atoms.reference: Seven decades of English-language outputs from computer generation systems; human–computer collaborations conceptually defined but not implemented as a computer system excluded.

evidence.record_quote: An anthology of seven decades of English-language outputs from computer generation systems, chronicling the vast history of machine-written texts created long before ChatGPT.
Purposefully excluded are human–computer collaborations that were conceptually defined but not implemented as a computer system.

atoms.reference: Outputs across creative writing, research-system text, reports and utilitarian texts, each excerpt introduced and organized by fine-grain genre; 500 pages.

evidence.record_quote: The outputs span many different types of creative writing and include text generated by research systems, along with reports and utilitarian texts, representing many general advances and experiments in text generation.

each of the excerpts is introduced individually and organized by fine-grain genre including conversations, humor, letters, poetry, prose, and sentences. Bibliographic references allow readers to learn more about outputs and systems that intrigue them.

atoms.reference: To correct the omission of the long history of text generation.

evidence.record_quote: aims to correct that omission by gathering seven decades of English-language texts produced by generation systems and software.

atoms.span: is a 504-page collection edited by Lillian-Yvonne Bertram and Nick Montfort.
Focuses strictly on functional computer-generated systems and software output, deliberately excluding pure human-computer conceptual collaborations.
Features 200 selections across fine-grained genres including poetry, prose, storytelling, conversations, humor, letters, reporting, rhetoric, and code.

observations.notes: An accurate composition of the book as a catalogue item, taken from MIT Press, whose date, length and price differ from the Counterpath page the census rests on. The exclusion rule loses its condition, and the book's argument against a recent origin of machine text is absent.
